hints.title: Combinatorial Jump Branching Obstacle
hints.text: Each array index specifies the maximum jump length forward. Testing every combination of jump lengths explores exponential possibilities. How can maintaining a single running bound of the farthest reachable index determine whether the final index is attainable?

hints.title: Max-Reach Invariant
hints.text: If the current index exceeds the maximum reach achievable so far, progress is halted. Otherwise, the maximum reach extends to max(current reach, i + nums[i]).

hints.title: Single-Pass Greedy Scan Procedure
hints.text: Initialize max_reach to 0. Iterate through each index i and value n. If i exceeds max_reach, return false immediately. Update max_reach as the maximum of max_reach and i + n. If max_reach is greater than or equal to the last index, return true. Return true after completing the loop.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of array nums (1 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Single forward pass updating a single reachability integer.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursively testing all possible jump lengths takes O(2^N) time, timing out on arrays with multiple zero or large jumps.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Greedy max-reach tracking delivers optimal O(N) time and O(1) space with no auxiliary arrays.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Early exit when current index exceeds max reach, early return when max reach reaches last index.
